claims.statement: Disabling repository-level self-hosted runner creation does not prevent workflows from accessing organization- or enterprise-level self-hosted runners. Creation restriction is not complete runner isolation.

Self-hosted runners are not guaranteed ephemeral clean VMs and can be compromised by untrusted workflows or fork pull requests, exposing secrets and GITHUB_TOKEN with settings-dependent write access. Environment reviews control secret release but do not isolate the runner.
Source presents disabling repository-level self-hosted runner creation as a possible risk response, not universal prohibition or permission to disable an estate capability.
Disabling Actions prevents repository workflows from running; it does not demonstrate security compliance or authorize disabling required capabilities.

Actions defaults enabled across organizations/repositories on FPT/GHEC, and on GHES after instance enablement. Scope permits enterprise versus organization disabling/limiting, conditionally including reusable workflows; default capability is not an observed setting.

Docker container actions, job containers and service containers require Linux runners; hosted branch specifies Ubuntu, self-hosted requires Linux with Docker installed. This prerequisite is not authority to install or start Docker.

Dockerfile action guidance documents required arguments in README, omits them from CMD, offers defaults requiring no args and uses an exposed help flag for self-documentation. Parent action context and actual usability still require testing.

Some listed domains resolve through CNAMEs; firewalls may need recursive rules for all CNAMEs, whose targets can change while listed domains remain stable. Parent domain list and actual firewall behavior are separate.
The enclosing CLI rerun supports --debug for runner diagnostic and step debug logs; this does not validate Azure CLI's separate malformed ---debug example or authorize rerunning jobs.
UI rerun optionally enables diagnostic and step debug logging before Re-run jobs; no rerun, data exposure or credential-bearing logging is authorized by source review.

Enabled Actions can run repository actions and conditionally reusable workflows, with FPT public and GHEC/GHES public/internal external repositories described. Capability statement does not override selected-action policy or actual access restrictions.

Organization owners may grant organization Actions usage-metric viewing through custom organization roles and the View organization Actions metrics permission; no role assigned or metrics access observed.
Enterprise storage procedure selects Azure Blob Storage Setup under Artifact & Log Storage; parent requirements, credentials and operational success are not established.

GHES Actions prerequisites include hardware review and configured domain TLS; self-signed-cert and HTTP-proxy reusable includes require separately resolved applicability/rendering. Links do not certify instance readiness.
Enterprise Actions procedure selects Enable GitHub Actions; this UI instruction is not permission for instance activation or evidence that workloads run.

GCP artifact/log storage fields include bucket service URL (usually https://storage.googleapis.com), bucket name and HMAC access ID/secret. Credential references are inert schema evidence; no secret generated, acquired or persisted.
Google Cloud Storage Setup appears under enterprise Artifact & Log Storage; selection alone does not establish authorized account/bucket configuration or storage health.
GHES conditional states dotcom-hosted runners unsupported and users should use self-hosted runners; this is platform-specific, not a universal self-hosted-only requirement.

When an HTTP proxy is configured, exclusion entries .localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 are required in that order; non-routable external storage additionally needs its URL excluded. No network setting changed or routing behavior verified.
After GitHub Connect enablement, enterprise policies may restrict allowed public actions; prerequisite and policy controls are distinct from actual enabled access or approved Connect activation.

GHES may have limited dotcom/Marketplace action access; source refers to access guidance and site administrator. Limited availability remains visible, not silently assumed absent, permitted or passing.
